system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer review — Project Kestrel

The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and efficiency note do **not** establish Buyer agreement. Review all positions. This review relies on the supplied summaries; the underlying SPA and DD documents still require verification. Monetary proposals below are Buyer negotiating positions, not agreed terms.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recourse proportionate to the risks, with protected categories outside the general cap. | **Counter:** open at **50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recoverability; do not concede 20% without compensating protection. **Reason:** the proposed cap leaves substantial acquisition risk with the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Individual claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; aggregate **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recoverable only above it. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; exclusions for protected categories. | **Counter:** propose **AUD 10,000 de minimis / AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, aggregating claims arising from related facts. **Reason:** the Seller’s combined thresholds can exclude meaningful losses and fragment related claims. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notify general warranty claims within **18 months**; extend limitations to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with separate periods for other categories and workable notice requirements. | **Counter:** seek 24 months, longer if diligence warrants; timely notified claims survive resolution, with no unduly short proceedings deadline. **Reason:** 18 months may not expose issues across two reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and time limit. | Separate protection for capacity, authority, ownership, valid issue and unencumbered transfer of all shares. | **Reject:** seek at least a **100% price cap / AUD 24m**, no de minimis or basket, and a longer expressly agreed period—e.g. seven years, with NSW enforceability checked. **Reason:** acquiring valid title is the transaction’s foundation, not an ordinary business risk. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to Claims of any nature; no express fraud protection is offered. | An express fraud/fraudulent misrepresentation carve-out across every relevant contractual restriction, without restricting non-excludable statutory rights. | **Reject blanket application:** carve fraud out of caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences, exclusive remedies and non-reliance; address attribution of Seller representatives’ fraud. **Reason:** the Seller should not obtain contractual protection for fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, Accounts, registers, public records and material “referred to” there. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the matter’s nature and scope; an immutable, indexed disclosure record. | **Reject blanket disclosure:** require specific warranty-linked disclosures, limit any agreed general disclosures, exclude unprovided cross-references, and preserve copies of the final disclosure set. **Reason:** access to documents is not equivalent to meaningful disclosure of a risk. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from records. | No constructive or imputed knowledge bar; preferably no knowledge exclusion at all. | **Delete**, or confine to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer deal-team members at signing, proved by Seller, without adviser attribution or a duty to investigate. **Reason:** “discoverable” shifts the Seller’s warranty risk onto Buyer diligence. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied upon delivery of written consent, although no final consent or satisfaction evidence is supplied. | A completion condition requiring effective consent and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions, without unacceptable commercial changes. | **Require a Buyer-waivable CP:** inspect clauses 11.2–11.3, approve the consent’s substance, verify all conditions and continuing effectiveness, and retain longstop/termination rights. **Reason:** written delivery alone does not protect a customer representing approximately 30% of revenue. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Debt repayment and effective release of security and relevant guarantees at Completion, consistent with debt-free/cash-free pricing. | **Reject unsecured post-completion release:** obtain a verified payout letter, direct repayment through funds flow and binding release arrangements effective at Completion, with registration discharge promptly evidenced. **Reason:** Buyer must not inherit secured debt or rely solely on Seller’s later performance. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses are a Seller matter and omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller-funded treatment of transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable on-costs, with correct payroll administration and no duplication in adjustments. | **Itemise and fund:** verify entitlements and conditions, calculate superannuation/payroll tax and other applicable costs, and deduct or fund the liability through agreed price mechanics, backed by an indemnity where needed. **Reason:** calling bonuses a Seller matter does not prevent the Company bearing the liability after Completion. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; transfer depends on cleared payment of all SOW3 fees; **AUD 180,000** recorded open. | Verified ownership of necessary IP, plus protection for losses arising from the identified ownership defect—not merely the unpaid invoice. | **Require cure before Completion:** reconcile and verify payment, obtain effective confirmatory assignment and necessary consents; retain a specific indemnity for resulting third-party claims, cure costs and business losses, outside general warranty limitations. **Reason:** paying an invoice alone may not establish complete IP ownership or remedy past exposure. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, said not to be material; possible export of approximately **1,240 records**, with access and notification obligations unresolved. | Urgent factual and legal assessment, containment, preserved evidence and allocation of pre-Completion incident exposure. | **Keep open:** require investigation updates, remediation covenants and a specific indemnity for attributable investigation, notification, response and third-party liabilities, to the extent legally recoverable; consider retention/security. **Reason:** uncertainty neither establishes a reportable breach nor justifies dismissing the risk. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Combined assessment of timing, scope, commitment, termination rights and accounting treatment. | **Verify before allocating:** read DD-008 and DD-011 together; control new commitments and adjust price only where justified by agreed debt/working-capital or leakage definitions. **Reason:** related renewals cannot be dismissed individually, but are not automatically debt-like merely because they exist. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, price adjustments and fraud. | **Redraft with explicit precedence:** state each category’s cap, period and applicable defences; prevent general boilerplate overriding specific protections, while avoiding double recovery. **Reason:** blanket drafting can silently neutralise separately negotiated remedies. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independent verification of the entire issued capital, ownership, transferability and absence of competing rights or security. | **Do not rely on the register alone:** reconcile corporate records, certificates and issue/transfer history; check options, convertibles, beneficial interests, transfer restrictions and relevant security searches; require releases and valid transfer/registration deliverables. **Reason:** a register entry does not establish every element of clean title. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled under the general regime. | Expressly negotiated tax protection and IP warranties appropriate to an analytics business, with identified risks separately addressed. | **Reopen:** seek a pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity with tailored exclusions and periods aligned to applicable assessment/reassessment windows plus a buffer; negotiate IP ownership, licensing, infringement and contractor-chain warranties with suitable caps and survival, preserving Ironquay protection. **Reason:** neither risk category should be deemed settled through generic limitations. |

**Completion priorities:** effective Bluefen consent, Riverlark payoff/release arrangements, funded bonus treatment and verified Ironquay IP cure. Keep the privacy investigation and tax/IP terms expressly open.

**Avoid overstating other consent requirements:** the supplied disclosures describe the office lease as requiring notification, not landlord consent, and Mossvale as restricting assignment—not necessarily a share sale. Verify the actual wording before imposing either consent requirement.
=== END ADVICE ===
